owner: akiendelllinux_cc_0 (CC) gates writes. Akien's idea, 2026-07-26: 'perhaps what we need is to build an inspector for the overall plan and intentions.'
intention: An inspector that reads the PLAN — the build order, the charters, and their filed edges — and reds the disagreements between them. Its first tooth: a component whose status reads DONE while its own filed_edges name an unbuilt dependency that downstream work is planned against.
why: MEASURED 2026-07-26, three instances of one defect, and the existing checks cannot see it because they check artifacts against artifacts. (1) inference_domain sits on the build order as done; its own filed edge (b) says 'THE HOST CLIENT is injected and not yet wired to a real host'; the librarian is planned on top of it. (2) db_domain filed edge (e): 'the FORWARD path ... proven possible by the seal stone but not yet wired end-to-end.' (3) The web server's live-render horizon waits on launcher wiring. In every case the COMPONENT-level record is honest — the filed edge states the truth plainly — and the PLAN-level reading is wrong, because nobody cross-read 'done' against the component's own list of what it does not do. Akien, on being shown it: 'even with all our checks we are still sitting on a MESS. that's why i wanted a sanity check!' The components are not a mess. The status accounting is.
traces_to: Law 3 — an unmeasured claim is a hypothesis. 'The spine is done up to the librarian' was a hypothesis presented as a position.

Law 5 — intent, its voyage and its proofs share an address. The evidence needed to catch all three cases was already AT the right address (each component's own filed_edges); what was missing was anything that read across them.
Law 7 — errors are loud at diagnostic surfaces. A component that is done-except-for-the-thing-it-exists-to-do is an error that is currently silent at every surface we look at.
Law 1 — once this inspector exists, the cross-read is compiled and nobody re-derives it per session.
state: code-seam@v1: THINKME -> TICKETME -> [BUILDME] -> PROVEME -> LEARNME -> PROVED   (CAST 2026-07-26 via /sorted; cursor at BUILDME. Leaf. Gate ran, not red — two distinctions recorded.)

gates.prove_gate: proof gate — the tester runs the proof and emits a VALIDATION.

falsifier: Run against the tree AS IT STANDS TODAY, the inspector must RED inference_domain — status done on the build order, filed edge (b) naming an unwired host, and downstream work (the librarian) planned on it. It must also red db_domain's edge (e). A run that returns clean on today's tree is a hollow build and fails, because we know by measurement that those two are true right now. Second clause: when a red is CLEARED (the host gets wired), the same run must go green for that component without the check being edited — a check that only ever reds is not measuring anything.
horizon: Re-read when the first red it raises is one WE DID NOT ALREADY KNOW ABOUT. Until then it is confirmed to reproduce known findings, which is necessary but is not yet evidence that it finds unknown ones.
distinctions_recorded: IT INSPECTS THE PLAN, NOT THE CODE. The tester proves that a component does what it claims; this reads whether the PLAN's account of a component matches the component's own account of itself. Different question, different surface, no overlap with the tester's teeth.

IT IS THE SAME MOVE AS THE LOG INTERPRETER, one layer up. Akien's diagnostic-logging method builds the instrument that compiles a diagnostic slice, and the review is done by READING the instrument's output. This is that shape applied to the plan: build the instrument, read its output, escalate only if the evidence does not resolve.
dependencies: BUILDME needs the charters and the build order, both of which exist and are readable. A SECOND tooth — 'a charter claiming an external resource must carry a re-runnable verify' — wants the host-seam schema, which is a separate open node; filed rather than built here.
provenance: Akien asked for a step-back sanity check on progress and floated an inspector for the overall plan and intentions. CC ran the sanity check by hand, found the done-vs-filed-edge pattern three times, and the inspector is the compiled form of the pass that found it — the hand-run becomes the instrument (Law 1).
filed_edges: SECOND TOOTH, NOT BUILT — a charter that claims an external resource (a host, a mount, a service) must carry a re-runnable VERIFY, because its implementation lives where git cannot see it and its seal expires as the host drifts. That is the host-seam pattern, and inference_domain's host connection IS a host-seam that was never treated as one. Wants the host-seam schema cast first.

THE BUILD ORDER LIVES IN MAP.md AS PROSE. This inspector has to read a human-written narrative to learn what the plan claims. That is fragile and is the real reason MAP.md is described as transitional. Filed: the build order wants a machine-readable form, and this inspector is the consumer that would pull it.
